comparison.objective: Insert two stemmed glasses through the open end of an overhead rack channel and leave them hanging upside down.
comparison.physical_skill: Grip fragile thin stems, lift each foot above the lips, thread the stem into an open-ended channel, slide and lower to hang; no bimanual butt-joint maintenance or free internal elements.
comparison.success_condition: Requires one or two glasses stably hanging with foot, stem and tilt tolerances and no knock-over; candidate requires rail-jig contact, parallel support throughout transfer and retention of all balls.
comparison.reason: This is the nearest geometric neighbor because both slide an object from an open end along a support channel. However, it tests high-reach placement and suspended seating of rigid stemware, while the candidate tests uninterrupted transfer of an uncaged recirculating bearing across a mated interface. Candidate maximum gap and angular tolerance are unpublished, but ball-loss and interface-separation gates make the abilities meaningfully different.
